claim_boundary: Each result verifies that one exact public statement appeared in the fetched WHO and UNICEF Immunization Coverage Estimates 2024 revision: methodology notes bytes on 2026-08-17. It does not independently establish the statement's underlying real-world truth.
review_design: retrospective deterministic source-publication audit; not preregistered, not an independent fact-check, and not an independent reproduction
source_name: WHO and UNICEF Immunization Coverage Estimates 2024 revision: methodology notes
selection_method: Deterministic sentence extraction with minimum length and prose-quality filters, signal scoring, duplicate removal, and per-page concentration limits.
verification_rule: Extract PDF text with the selecting extractor and an independent extractor, compare each quote after removing layout whitespace and hyphens, require every quote once or more in both extractions, and require the complete fetched PDF SHA-256 to match.

records.public_claim_text: Response levels from countries remains high, with 188 of 195 reports from WHO/UNICEF Member States received; 185 with coverage data (representing 95% of the global birth cohort), as of 21 June 2026.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: Response levels from countries remains high, with 188 of 195 reports from WHO/UNICEF Member States received; 185 with coverage data (representing 95% of the global birth cohort), as of 21 June 2026.

records.public_claim_text: Caution: Estimates do not correct retrospectively for any catch-up doses, therefore coverage for the cohorts might be underestimated, thus the number of un- and under vaccinated for years before 2025 might have declined.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: Caution: Estimates do not correct retrospectively for any catch-up doses, therefore coverage for the cohorts might be underestimated, thus the number of un- and under vaccinated for years before 2025 might have declined.

records.public_claim_text: As not all nationally representative household surveys include children aged 24-35 months, the cohort most appropriate for measuring MCV2 coverage, MCV2 coverage estimates are often informed by nationally reported coverage data.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: As not all nationally representative household surveys include children aged 24-35 months, the cohort most appropriate for measuring MCV2 coverage, MCV2 coverage estimates are often informed by nationally reported coverage data.

records.public_claim_text: Beginning with the 2013 revision (completed in July 2014), WHO and UNICEF produce coverage estimates for the hepatitis B birth dose from 2000 onwards for countries where the vaccine dose is recommended in the national immunization schedule for universal use and where empirical data are available for at least one year since introduction in the schedule.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: Beginning with the 2013 revision (completed in July 2014), WHO and UNICEF produce coverage estimates for the hepatitis B birth dose from 2000 onwards for countries where the vaccine dose is recommended in the national immunization schedule for universal use and where empirical data are available for at least one year since introduction in the schedule.

records.public_claim_text: An assumption is made that countries who were able to distinguish birth doses from late doses as of 2016 were able to do so prior to this performance year.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: An assumption is made that countries who were able to distinguish birth doses from late doses as of 2016 were able to do so prior to this performance year.

records.public_claim_text: Beginning with the 2023 revision (completed in July 2024), WHO and UNICEF produce coverage estimates for at least one dose of meningococcal A conjugate vaccine (MengA) from 2016 onwards for countries where at least one dose of meningococcal A conjugate vaccine is recommended in the national infant schedule and who reported data to WHO and UNICEF.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: Beginning with the 2023 revision (completed in July 2024), WHO and UNICEF produce coverage estimates for at least one dose of meningococcal A conjugate vaccine (MengA) from 2016 onwards for countries where at least one dose of meningococcal A conjugate vaccine is recommended in the national infant schedule and who reported data to WHO and UNICEF.

records.public_claim_text: Beginning with the 2015 revision, WHO and UNICEF produce coverage estimates for rubella-containing vaccine for those countries where the vaccine is included in the national immunization schedule.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: Beginning with the 2015 revision, WHO and UNICEF produce coverage estimates for rubella-containing vaccine for those countries where the vaccine is included in the national immunization schedule.

records.public_claim_text: Reported immunization service delivery performance data were received through the Joint Reporting Form on Immunization by 21 June 2026 from 188 of 195 WHO/UNICEF Member States; 185 included coverage data.
records.public_claim_verbatim_quote: Reported immunization service delivery performance data were received through the Joint Reporting Form on Immunization by 21 June 2026 from 188 of 195 WHO/UNICEF Member States; 185 included coverage data.

records.public_claim_text: Rules for survey inclusion / exclusion Final survey reports that were either publicly reported and available or those received from countries by the WHO and UNICEF working group by 21 June 2026 were included in the 2025 revision of the WUENIC, sent to countries for review and comment.
